subject: Money
title: The Dot-Com Bubble
description: A quick, practical guide to The Dot-Com Bubble.

hook.text: Yahoo was worth more than the entire U.S. steel industry in 1999. It had 3,000 employees and no profits.

buildup.text: The internet was genuinely revolutionary. But investors treated every website like the next Microsoft.

discovery.text: Companies added '.com' to their names and stock prices doubled. Actual business models were optional.

twist.text: Amazon survived the crash, falling 93% before becoming a trillion-dollar company. Most others simply vanished.

climax.text: The dot-com bubble destroyed $5 trillion in market value. But the internet it funded changed everything.

punchline.text: The technology was real. The valuations weren't.

quiz.question: How much did Amazon's stock fall during the dot-com crash?
